Mathlib informalized › Mathlib.Logic.Function

Mathlib.Logic.Function

Statements of Mathlib (commit a88727a581), each with its Lean source, its translation to Dedukti by Export.lean, and its informalization by Informath, in English, as a formula, and in French, Czech, German and Swedish, which the buttons at each entry show there, and the check boxes above the entries everywhere. The Dedukti translation drops implicit and instance arguments and maps Lean's arithmetic and logic to Informath's base (mapping.tsv); the other Mathlib constants are worded by the symbol table mathlib.dkgf, whose English wordings Informath also renders in the other languages. Constants without a wording appear as $\mathrm{name}$.

Function.evaldefBasic.lean:35
Evaluate a function at an argument. Useful if you want to talk about the partially applied Function.eval x : (∀ x, β x) → β x.
Lean
@[reducible, simp] def eval {β : α → Sort*} (x : α) (f : ∀ x, β x) : β x := f x
Dedukti
2 lines
def Function__eval : (X : Set) -> (x : (Elem X -> Set)) -> (x1 : Elem X) -> (f : ((x2 : Elem X) -> x x2)) -> Elem (x x1) :=
  X => x => x1 => f => f x1.
English
Let $X$ be a set. Let $x$ be a function from elements of $X$ to sets. Let $x_{1} \in X$. Let $f$ be a function from elements $x_{2}$ of $X$ to elements of $x (x_{2})$. Then the evaluation of $X$ and $x$ is an element of $x (x_{1})$ defined as the function that maps $f$ to $x_{2} (x_{1} , f)$.
French
Soit $X$ un ensemble. Soit $x$ une fonction des éléments de $X$ à des ensembles. Soit $x_{1} \in X$. Soit $f$ une fonction des éléments $x_{2}$ de $X$ à des éléments de $x (x_{2})$. Alors l'évaluation de $X$ et $x$ est un élément de $x (x_{1})$ défini comme la fonction qui envoie $f$ sur $x_{2} (x_{1} , f)$.
Czech
Nechť $X$ je množina. Nechť $x$ je funkce z prvků z $X$ do množin. Nechť $x_{1} \in X$. Nechť $f$ je funkce z prvků $x_{2}$ z $X$ do prvků z $x (x_{2})$. Tedy vyhodnocení $X$ a $x$ je prvek z $x (x_{1})$ definovaný jako funkce která zobrazuje $f$ na $x_{2} (x_{1} , f)$.
Formula
$X \in \mathrm{Set} , x \in X \rightarrow \mathrm{Set} , x_{1} \in X , f \in X \rightarrow x (x_{2})\vdash \operatorname{eval} (X , x , x_{1} , x_{2} , f):= \lambda f . x_{2} (x_{1} , f)\in x (x_{1})$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $f$ be a surjective function from elements of $X$ to elements of $Y$. Let $p$ be a function from elements of $Y$ to propositions. Then there exists an element $y$ of $Y$, such that $p (y)$, if and only if there exists an element $x$ of $X$, such that $p (f (x))$.

Function.not_surjective_TypetheoremBasic.lean:386
There is no surjection from α : Type u into Type (max u v). This theorem demonstrates why Type : Type would be inconsistent in Lean.
Lean
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

    have hpi : partialInv f b = if h : ∃ a, f a = b then some (Classical.choose h) else none :=

            apply Classical.choose_spec h'

Function.rec_updatetheoremBasic.lean:748
Recursors can be pushed inside Function.update.
The ctor argument should be a one-argument constructor like Sum.inl, and recursor should be an inductive recursor partially applied in all but that constructor, such as (Sum.rec · g).
In future, we should build some automation to generate applications like Option.rec_update for all inductive types.

Function.extenddefBasic.lean:841
Extension of a function g : α → γ along a function f : α → β.
For every a : α, f a is sent to g a. f might not be surjective, so we use an auxiliary function j : β → γ by sending b : β not in the range of f to j b. If you do not care about the behavior outside the range, j can be used as a junk value by setting it to be 0 or Classical.arbitrary (assuming γ is nonempty).
This definition is mathematically meaningful only when f a₁ = f a₂ → g a₁ = g a₂ (spelled g.FactorsThrough f). In particular this holds if f is injective.
A typical use case is extending a function from a subtype to the entire type. If you wish to extend g : {b : β // p b} → γ to a function β → γ, you should use Function.extend Subtype.val g j.
Lean
def extend (f : α → β) (g : α → γ) (j : β → γ) : β → γ := fun b ↦
  open scoped Classical in
  if h : ∃ a, f a = b then g (Classical.choose h) else j b
